item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
528
ABPZ20 KNHC 021125
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Fri Oct 2 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Nolo, located several hundred miles west-northwest of Lihue,
Hawaii, and on Hurricane Rachel, located a couple of hundred miles
south of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form late this weekend or
early next week south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development,
and a tropical depression is likely to form by the middle of next
week while the system moves slowly west-northwestward to
northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.description:

000
WTPZ33 KNHC 020833

BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM MST Fri Oct 02 2026
 
...RACHEL WEAKENS SLIGTHLY AS IT TURNS WESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.4N 110.4W
ABOUT 245 MI...390 KM S OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...115 MPH...185 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...955 MB...28.20 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 19.4 North, longitude 110.4 West. Rachel is moving
toward the west near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this motion is expected to
continue into the weekend. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 115 mph (185 km/h) with higher
gusts. Rachel is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale. Rachel is expected to remain near its current 
intensity today, followed by gradual weakening during the next 
couple of days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 955 mb (28.20 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will affect the coast of 
west-central Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula through the 
weekend. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and 
rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local 
weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 21
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Fri Oct 02 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 020836
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM MST Fri Oct 02 2026
 
Rachel's satellite presentation has degraded somewhat over the past 
several hours, with the eye becoming obscured in conventional 
satellite imagery and some mid-level dry air entraining into the 
northeastern portion of the circulation. However, recent microwave 
imagery indicates that the inner-core structure remains intact. A 
0429 UTC METOP-B scatterometer pass helped refine the wind radii and 
structure. The latest Dvorak Data-T estimate from TAFB decreased to 
4.5/77 kt, with objective intensity estimates ranging from 87 to 104 
kt. Given these estimates and the degraded satellite presentation, 
the initial intensity is lowered to 100 kt.
 
The initial motion is westward, or 270/4 kt, and this motion is 
expected to continue with a gradual increase in forward speed over 
the weekend and into early next week as a mid-level ridge builds to 
the north. A gradual bend toward the west-northwest is forecast 
between 72 and 96 h as the ridge begins to weaken. The track 
guidance remains in decent agreement on this scenario, although some 
differences remain in the timing of the increase in forward speed 
by early next week. The latest NHC track forecast is similar to the 
previous prediction and lies near the HCCA and GDMI aids.
 
Although modest east-northeasterly shear and some dry mid-level air 
are currently influencing the convective structure, environmental 
conditions largely remain favorable for Rachel to remain near its 
current intensity during the next 12 h, especially while the 
inner-core structure remains intact. Thereafter, increasingly dry 
mid-level air is forecast to begin wrapping into the system, while 
some east-northeasterly shear could persist. These factors should 
gradually disrupt the inner-core structure and induce a weakening 
trend. Increasingly marginal sea surface temperatures later in the 
forecast period should support continued weakening through day 5. 
The latest NHC intensity forecast is essentially unchanged from the 
previous advisory, showing Rachel holding steady over the next 12 h 
and then gradually weakening thereafter. This intensity forecast 
remains near the upper end of the guidance envelope through the 
forecast period.
